messages.subject: Bug in CopyObjects
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I discovered a bug in RHIPE. If call rhwatch like

simul <- rhwatch(map=coderunner, input=c(length(mygrid),50), reduce=0, setup=expression({
    suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))
    load("foo.Rdata")
})
                 ,jobname='Hr Usage Sampler'
                 ,mapred=list(mapred.task.timeout=0)
                 ,shared="/user/sguha/tmp/foo.Rdata"
                 )

foo is a 64MB file, i didn't want RHIPE to automaticall copy objects
referenced from coderunner, so i also did

rho <- rhoptions()$copy
rho$auto <- FALSE
rhoptions(copyObjects=rho)

and instead saved all the objects in foo.Rdata.

coderunner looks like function(a,b) ....

When copyObjects is FALSE,i get the following error:

Error in match.fun(FUN) : object 'rhipe_inner_runner' not found

Because copyObjects is FALSE, the code is not getting copied. However if
copyObjects is TRUE(and i then remove the redundant shared param), then it does work, but there is the cost in startup
time because RHIPE copies all the objects to temporary file ...

In general copyObjects, though useful, could do with improvements. In
addition to the above, functions referenced from within functions dont
get copied ...

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: Comparing two large lists in Rhipe/Hadoop
messages.subject_clean: Comparing two large lists in Rhipe/Hadoop
messages.body_plain:
It depends on how big the small list is Ashrith.

If the small list is small enough to be replicated for every map or reduce instance it is called a replicated inner join, and you leave the large list on the hdfs (potentially huge).  The large list becomes the source of key/value pairs for MapReduce.

If the small list is not small enough to be replicated to every map instance.  The problem gets harder.  Occasionally you can trim down that small list until it can be or reduce the number of MapReduces running simultaneously to make it feasible.  It is a numbers game with simultaneous mappers X amount of memory the small list needs.

It is by no means an insurmountable problem if the small list can only be replicated once per a machine, but you are then outside of my experience.

 If you can't get the small list into any worker nodes memory because it is to large you are then in the difficult case and well outside my experience.

Thanks,
Jeremiah

I tried that Jeremiah. But both the lists are considerably big so could
not attempt to tackle the problem that way.

Another method I thought of was to take each element of the smaller list
and compare it to the larger list and spin each of these off as a job.
This, although might be good for my lists, the number of jobs
made me queasy along with the fact  that it was be computationally infeasible.

One of the biggest advantages that I had was a common source for both
the list. One of the things I at least tend to forget is that while using
MR and Rhipe you almost lose one dimension of operation, so you have to
write your code in a "linear" way. So I tried the problem this way.

List A had to satisfy some condition (x==y) and B had to satisfy another
(q==b). And then I had to compare how many from A occured in B, or the
other way.

For this I used some flags and also used the common data source.

t2r$input <- "common data source"

In my map process I used

if(x==y){rhcollect(valueforlist1,1)}
else if(a == b){rhcollect(valueforlist2,2)

Now if both the conditions are met then both 1 and 2 are emitted from two
different elements of the list.

So now if I had to check if elements in list 1 were in list 2 all I had
to do is to look for values that had both the flags, 1 and 2,
respectively.

t2r$reduce <- expression(
        pre = {
                        final.vec <- vector()
                }
        ,reduce = {
                        temp.vec <- unlist(reduce.values)
                        final.vec <- c(final.vec,temp.vec)
                }
        ,post = {
                        if(length(final.vec) > 1 && '1' %in% final.vec && '2' %in% final.vec){
                        rhcollect(reduce.key,table(final.vec))
                                        }
                }
)

So this eventually was just one job and I was able to figure out element
matches of these two lists.

Mabbe this would help if someone has a similar problem.

messages.subject: Strategy for chaining map/reduce jobs
messages.body_plain:
Is there a recommended strategy for chaining map/reduce jobs in RHIPE? I have an algorithm split into steps, each of them map/reduce, each step taking output of previous step as it’s input.

The first idea I got is

step1 <- rhwatch(…)

rhwrite(step1, “step1OutPath”)

step2 <- rhwatch(… input=rhfmst(“step1OutPath”, ..)… )

The second idea is to explicitly write into hdfs in reduce steps.

Is there a recommendation for this?

Thanks
   Ondra Nekola

messages.body_plain:
So, typically this

step1 = rhwatch(..., read=FALSE)

## was step1 successful?

wasSuccess <- m2[[1]]$rerrors == FALSE &&length(m2[[1]]$errors)==0 &&
m2[[1]]$state=="SUCCEEDED"

(i'm using everything, i'm not sure if one is equivalent to all 3 ...!)

if(wasSuccess) step2 = rhwatch(..., input=step1,...)

if the step{N-1} was successfull

rhwatch(..., input=Step{N-1}, output="final-destination") ...

Done.

Hope it helps. jobs with no output parameter will create temporary
folders in rhoptions()$HADOOP.TMP.FOLDER . You can delete them using
rhclean() (dont run the latter command when your other jobs are
running ...)
